sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:1
items.html: The Nekudot are divided into three parts: which are according to the three lights, Bina, ZA and Malchut, that shine in the Nekudim, as above (413, the passage beginning “Now you will understand”). For there is there the light of Bina in the discernment of clothing, which is called male, and which is the Keter of the Nekudim. And there is there a level of phase one, which is the female of the Nekudim, called Hochma and Bina, where the light of ZA is in Hochma and the light of Malchut is in Bina. Study it there well. And this is what he says, that the Nekudot are divided into three parts, which are Bina, ZA and Malchut, clothed in the Keter, Hochma and Bina of the Nekudot. However, know that the ZA and Malchut that are in Hochma and Bina are both considered one part, since they are the discernment of the light of a single level, which is the level of phase one. And therefore the seven lower Sefirot are regarded as the third part. Thus the Keter, which has Bina in the discernment of clothing, is the upper part; and Hochma and Bina, both together, are the second part; and the ZAT are the third part.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:2
items.html: The Holam is the vapour that comes out from the Tabur, where the Keter stands. Which is the light of Bina in the discernment of clothing, as above. And it was explained above (page 412, the passage beginning “And from here,” and on page 413, the passage beginning “And here the male”) that from this coupling of phase two of clothing no expansion of vessels came out at all, for there is no expansion of vessels except from a screen that has in it the discernment of drawing. See there. Therefore the vessels came out only from phase one of the female, which are Hochma and Bina. See there. And this is what he says, that the vapour that comes out from the Tabur to the Keter of the Nekudim — and this vapour is the light of Bina, as above (page 420, item 27, in the words of the ARI) — is the discernment of the Holam that is above the letters. For the letters are the vessels, as above, and this light of Bina, which came out only from phase two of clothing, has no expansion into vessels; and therefore it is the discernment of the Holam that is above the letters and does not touch them, since it cannot clothe within them.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:3
items.html: The Shuruk in the Vav, which is called Melafum, which is in the middle. As written above, that only AVI, who are the female of the Nekudim, have an expansion of vessels and are able to clothe within them. And therefore AVI are alluded to in the Shuruk, that is, the Melafum, which is in the middle of the letters.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:4
items.html:
The Yod of the Shuruk is for Aba, who is called the first Yod of the name. That is, the Yod of the name HaVaYaH, which is the discernment of AB, which is Aba, as is known. And it alludes to the discernment of the five Hassadim of the Yesod that Aba takes.
For the bestowal of the Yesod is only the Hassadim and the Gvurot, as is known, and Aba takes the five Hassadim, since AB is the secret of Hassadim.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:5
items.html: And the Vav, etc., is for Ima, to bring out and beget the VAK [six ends] of ZA. Ima is the secret of the first Hey of the name HaVaYaH, and therefore she received from the Yesod the discernment of the truncated Vav that is inside the Hey, which is her MAN [female waters], and which is the secret of the ZA in the womb of Bina.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:6
items.html: The point, etc., and from it Aba of the Nekudim nurses. The point alludes to the bottom Hey that rose to the Nikvey Einayim, from where AVI of the Nekudim came out, as above; and she has now become a discernment of MAN for Aba, for the secret of the great coupling of the look of the Einayim of AVI, as written below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:7
items.html: And the Vav of the Shuruk, from it Ima of the Nekudim nurses: This is in the manner of what is written in Etz Chaim, Gate 8, Chapter 1, that by the force of the ascent of the MAN to the Nikvey Einayim, he divides there the HaVaYaH of SAG, whose Vav is in the Peh, which is Ima. See there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:8
items.html: The Nekudot are Hochma and the letters are Bina. For AVI, from the beginning of their emanation, have in them only the level of ZA; and Aba is regarded as the light of ZA, and Ima as the vessel, which is the secret of the letters. And this light of the Katnut is called by the name the light of the Nekudot, as above in the words of the ARI, in item 30 here. And this is what he says: the Nekudot are Hochma and the letters are Bina.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:9
items.html:
And the seven lower Nekudot, etc., these ten that came out through the nails of the feet. That is, they are the Nekudot that are beneath the letters, which are nine Nekudot; and in the first two Nekudot among them, the Kamatz and the Patach, there was no breaking, for they are Keter and Hochma. Thus they are seven lower Nekudot, in which there was the breaking of the vessels, as the ARI writes in Etz Chaim, Gate 8, Chapter 1. See there. And these nine Nekudot are lower, beneath the letters, because they received the discernment of the vapours that come out through the nails of the feet, which are beneath the vessels of the Partzuf. And one should not object that he says above that the Holam and the Shuruk are the Keter and Hochma, that is, the upper and the middle Nekudot, whereas here he counts them as Kamatz and Patach, so that the Keter and Hochma too turn out to be lower Nekudot. And the matter is that one must distinguish in them between the essence of their emanation — that is, as they first came out through the Nikvey Einayim, where only two lights came out, which are male and female, the Keter being the secret of the male, whose level reaches up to Bina in the discernment of clothing, and the female being Hochma and Bina, both together, which are in the level of phase one, as above. And therefore they are regarded here as Holam and Shuruk, to indicate that the male, which is Keter, has no expansion into vessels, and is therefore found above the Partzuf, in the secret of the point of the Tabur, which is above the Partzuf of Nekudim; and this is the discernment of the Holam, which is a Keter to the letters and does not enter into the expansion of the Partzuf. However, corresponding to this, AVI are alluded to in the Shuruk, which is inside the letters, that is, inside the Partzuf, since they are the discernment of the female, who have complete MAN also from the discernment of drawing, as above.
However, the Nekudot that are beneath the letters allude to the time of the Gadlut of the Nekudim, after AB and SAG coupled, and the level that came out through their coupling descended and breached the Parsa — meaning that the boundary of the Sium of the feet of SAG was annulled. And then the whole Partzuf of the Nekudim, which stands beneath the Parsa, received from the feet of SAG that are above the Parsa; that is, the ten Sefirot of the Sium of SAG, upon which the Parsa rides, now attained discernments of expansion and shone to the Nekudim. And it turns out that the Nekudim now receive from the lights that are below the Partzuf relative to the previous state, and these are what are called the Nekudot that are beneath the letters. And understand well, that that very discernment of the Holam, which is above the letters of the Partzuf of Nekudim from the standpoint of the essence of its emanation, descended from there at the time of the Gadlut and clothed in the Nekudim, that is, inside the letters. And we call them “beneath the letters” only relative to the state of the giver, and not relative to the state of the receiver.
Now it has been explained that the Keter and Hochma too received from the Sium of the feet of SAG, like the ZAT; and indeed it is they who received them primarily, and it is they who bestowed them upon the ZAT, as written below. And from this standpoint they are called Kamatz and Patach, which are beneath the letters. Thus, in order to mark the discernment of Keter and Hochma from the essence of their emanation, they are marked by Holam and Shuruk; and when they are marked from the standpoint of what they received through the Gadlut of the Nekudim, they are then designated by the name Kamatz and Patach. However, what the ARI writes, that the Kamatz and Patach were not broken, refers to what they have from the standpoint of the essence of their emanation, and not to what they received from the Sium of the feet of SAG, for those illuminations were annulled from the Keter and Hochma as well, as written below. And they are called by the name the lights of the posterior of AVI.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:31:10
items.html: And it is not our intention to say that these are the Nekudot themselves. That is, that those lights and vapours that came out from the nails of his feet are not the self of the Nekudot, but they are regarded as a discernment of addition alone; for the discernment of the self of the Nekudot came out from the light of the Einayim, as above.
